## 1. When flexibility helps

For each situation, say whether a flexible method would generally
outperform an inflexible one, and justify your answer using the reducible
and irreducible error decomposition from lecture.

a. The sample size n is extremely large, and the number of predictors p is small.
b. The number of predictors p is extremely large, and the number of observations n is small.
c. The true relationship between the predictors and the response is highly non-linear.
d. The variance of the error term, $\text{Var}(\varepsilon)$, is extremely large.

## 2. Parametric or not

a. Describe the difference between a parametric and a non-parametric approach to estimating f.
b. Name one advantage and one disadvantage of the parametric approach, relative to the non-parametric one.
c. ISLP Figure 2.7 places methods on a plane with flexibility on one axis and interpretability on the other. Explain why those two axes point in opposite directions instead of varying independently.
d. A colleague wants to know exactly how each predictor moves the response, and also wants the most accurate predictions possible. Explain why they may not get both, and which one they should give up first.

## 3. Regression, classification, prediction, inference

For each scenario, say whether it is a regression or classification
problem, whether the goal is prediction or inference, and report n and p.

a. Data on the top 500 firms in the US, recording profit, number of employees, industry, and CEO salary, collected to understand which factors affect CEO salary.
b. Data on 20 previously launched products, recording whether each succeeded or failed along with price, marketing budget, competition price, and ten other variables, collected to predict whether a new product will succeed.
c. Weekly percent changes in the USD/Euro exchange rate and in the US, British, and German stock markets, recorded for all of 2012, collected to predict the USD/Euro change from the market changes.

## 4. Naming your own

Describe two real-life applications where classification is the right
framing, and two where regression is. For each, name the response, at
least two predictors, and say whether the goal is prediction or inference,
with a one-sentence justification.

a. A classification application.
b. A second classification application.
c. A regression application.
d. A second regression application.
